# Terraform-Generated Test Environment

## Overview
The `.env` file for smoke tests is now automatically generated by Terraform using the `local_file` resource. This eliminates manual configuration and ensures test environment matches deployed infrastructure.

## Implementation

### Location
`deploy/azure/infrastructure/helm.tf`

### Resource Definition
```hcl
resource "local_file" "test_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/../tests/.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
    # Service IPs for deployed services
    # Automatically generated by Terraform

    # MCP API Key for authentication
    MCP_API_KEY=${random_password.mcp_api_key.result}

    # Service IPs (LoadBalancer external IPs)
    MCP_VISUALIZATION_IP=${azurerm_public_ip.mcp_visualization_generator.ip_address}
    MCP_PUBLIC_FARMER_IP=${azurerm_public_ip.mcp_public_farmer_tools.ip_address}
    MCP_CHEF_SERVICES_IP=${azurerm_public_ip.mcp_chef_services.ip_address}

    # API Services (ClusterIP - for internal access only)
    API_STOCK_IP=10.0.0.1
  EOT

  depends_on = [helm_release.demo]
}
```

## Benefits

### 1. Zero Manual Configuration
- No need to run `kubectl get svc` and copy IPs
- No need to extract secrets from Kubernetes
- No need to manually edit `.env` file

### 2. Consistency
- Test environment always matches deployed infrastructure
- Static IPs are known before deployment (no waiting for LoadBalancer assignment)
- MCP API key is the same one used by deployed services

### 3. Automation-Friendly
- CI/CD pipelines can run tests immediately after `terraform apply`
- No additional scripts needed (no `generate_env.py`)
- Idempotent - rerunning terraform updates `.env` if IPs change

### 4. Single Source of Truth
- All configuration in Terraform
- No drift between infrastructure and test configuration
- Easy to see what tests are using

## Workflow

### Deploy Infrastructure
```powershell
cd deploy/azure/infrastructure
terraform apply
```

This automatically:
1. Creates static public IPs
2. Deploys Helm chart with static IP bindings
3. Generates `.env` file with:
   - Static LoadBalancer IPs
   - Generated MCP API key
   - Service endpoints

### Run Tests
```powershell
cd ../tests
uv run python main.py
```

Tests run immediately with correct configuration.

## Output Files

### Generated File Location
`deploy/azure/tests/.env`

### Format
```properties
# Service IPs for deployed services
# Automatically generated by Terraform
# DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY - Changes will be overwritten

# MCP API Key for authentication
MCP_API_KEY=<32-char-random-key>

# Service IPs (LoadBalancer external IPs)
MCP_VISUALIZATION_IP=<static-ip>
MCP_PUBLIC_FARMER_IP=<static-ip>
MCP_CHEF_SERVICES_IP=<static-ip>

# API Services (ClusterIP - for internal access only)
API_STOCK_IP=10.0.0.1
```

## Terraform Output

New output added for verification:
```hcl
output "test_env_file" {
  description = "Path to generated .env file for tests"
  value       = local_file.test_env.filename
}
```

View with:
```powershell
terraform output test_env_file
```

## Dependency Chain

```
azurerm_public_ip.* 
    ↓
helm_release.demo (uses static IPs)
    ↓
local_file.test_env (waits for deployment)
```

The `.env` file is only created after successful Helm deployment, ensuring services are running before tests are attempted.

## Migration Note

If you have an existing manually-created `.env` file, it will be overwritten by Terraform on next apply. Save any custom configuration before running `terraform apply`.
